svg.text: How the system works, step by step
Left: each stage with its input (IN), output (OUT) and job. Right: a plain-words analogy. Tag shows whether it came from the paper or is ours.
a photo or video frame uploaded in the browser (any size, e.g. 1000 x 800 pixels)
the same picture as numbers: height x width x 3 colour values (red, green, blue)
Analogy: the evidence on the table
A computer sees a picture as a big grid of
looks for a human face and 468 landmarks (eyes, nose, mouth, jaw)
a cropped face with a margin, or the whole image if no face is found; a flag "is it a face?"
Analogy: pick the right area to inspect
The paper's detector is built for faces. If it is a
landscape or a cat, we keep the whole image.
the crop resized to 336 x 336 x 3
cuts the image into 14 x 14 pixel patches (24 x 24 = 576 patches) and describes each one
576 patch vectors of 1024 numbers, taken at layers 8, 16 and -2, plus one whole-image vector (CLS)
CLIP was trained on millions of image + caption
pairs, so its patch descriptions carry meaning:
"this looks like skin", "this looks like fur".
3. M2F2 detector (the paper's own, kept frozen)
(a) text branch: learned "forgery prompts" give each patch a score = 576 numbers, a 24 x 24 map
(b) DenseNet-121 looks at the pixels for a second opinion; (c) a linear layer combines them
2 numbers: how "real" and how "fake"; plus the 24 x 24 score map and a DenseNet feature
This is what M2F2-Det already did: one real/fake
answer for faces. We keep it as a teacher and as
an input, but do not trust it alone.
4. Our forensic heads (trained in Stage A)
CLIP layers 8, 16, -2 (three zoom levels), the score map, DenseNet features
FPN mask decoder merges the three layers and paints two masks: where it was edited (forgery),
and where a filter was applied (processing); a pixel value near 1 means "edited here"
type head: probabilities for real, face swap, splice, diffusion inpainting, img2img, fully generated
filter head: yes/no for beauty, blur, JPEG, colour, sharpen, resize
from real edit masks (OpenForensics, DiffusionFace, CASIA, SD_inpaint) and by copying the paper's detector
The paper only said "fake". These heads say
FILTERS, because they were taught with the
5. Packing the evidence for the language model
the detector's 2 numbers go through a small layer (2 -> 4096 numbers): one special token (paper)
one 16-number token: real/fake (2), types (6), filters (6), edited-area share, filtered-area share (ours)
3 tokens of 1024 numbers: average CLIP patch inside the edited area, outside it, and in the filtered area
a short sentence built by rules, e.g. "The forensic heads indicate splicing; the heatmap marks the middle right (5%)"
The writer (LLM) cannot read masks. So we turn
the findings into tokens (numbers it understands)
and one plain sentence it can read.
the image as 576 tokens (LLaVA does this itself) + our tokens + the text: hint + "Is this image real or fake? Explain why."
a 7-billion-parameter language model predicts the answer one word at a time
Stage B: only the connector layer is trained. Stage C: the model is fine-tuned with QLoRA (4-bit, small add-on weights)
a paragraph: verdict, edit type, where, what looks wrong
The writer was taught from 100,000s of examples
to say things like "the cat's face was pasted in,
in the middle right". It copies the heatmap's place.
7. The UI decides, shows and checks
fake if the heads' fake probability is 0.5 or more (the LLM only explains it)
verdict, type, red heatmap, blue filter map, explanation, detected face
banner "uncertain" if signals disagree; checks the text's location, size and lighting against the heatmap
The heads are more accurate than the writer, so
they give the verdict. The checks catch sentences
Train the forensic heads (and the high-res branch in v5/v6) on images with real masks. The detector and CLIP stay as they are.
Data: OpenForensics, DiffusionFace, CASIA, SD_inpaint, DDVQA, FakeClue
Teach the connector layers to feed our tokens to LLaVA. LLaVA itself is frozen. Starts from the paper's projector so nothing breaks.
Fine-tune LLaVA with QLoRA so it writes explanations naming the edit type and the marked region. About 14 hours on the RTX 3060.
Data: DDVQA, MMTD-Set, FakeClue, teacher region names; lighting boilerplate removed
